name: Rlhf Flaw Is Institutional
text: TypeSafe's case for Jev locates RLHF's flaw in the human in the loop. Kaal's position is that the flaw is institutional: whoever supplies the reward signal bears no consequence for being wrong. A model that labels in the annotator's place loses nothing either. Replacing the human does not fix it; giving the signal a price does.
scope_conditions: TypeSafe's post announces a product. It is not an empirical test of these claims.
The position is Kaal's own argument in the essay After RLHF Comes a Stack, Not a Model.
The position does not evaluate Jev's accuracy, which TypeSafe has not published a calibration figure for.
The accountable-validation layer is proposed, not tested: no policy has yet been trained under it.
